children: A draft proof of the Riemann hypothesis produced with the help of artificial intelligence has reignited debate over Bitcoin’s security. Crypto research firm K33 said AI’s progress in mathematics bears watching, but there is no evidence the latest work has broken Bitcoin’s cryptographic system.

Levente Alfoldi, a mathematician at Anthropic, said on Nov. 20 that he had found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis using the AI model Claude. The Riemann hypothesis is a 167-year-old unsolved problem about the distribution of prime numbers. The published proof passed computer verification by independent researchers, and academic review is under way.

The advance raised concerns that AI could also solve the mathematical problems that underpin Bitcoin’s security. Bitcoin uses elliptic curve cryptography to sign transactions. The system relies on the idea that generating a public key from a private key is easy, while deriving the private key from the public key alone is extremely difficult.
One broader problem that could affect cryptography is P versus NP. It asks whether problems whose answers can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly.

K33 said a proof of the Riemann hypothesis does not provide a way to derive a private key from a public key. Even if that broader question were answered in the affirmative, it would not immediately deliver a practical algorithm or sufficient computing speed for real-world use. K33 added that P versus NP remains unsolved. There is no basis to conclude that recent advances in mathematics have broken Bitcoin’s cryptographic system.

The crypto industry is also moving to strengthen defenses. The Ethereum Foundation said AI is a more urgent threat than quantum computing because it can rapidly identify software vulnerabilities. The foundation plans to double the size of its protocol security team and shift by 2029 to a cryptographic system that can withstand attacks from quantum computers. It recommended Keccak-256 as the hash function for the new system.

title: Could AI Crack Bitcoin? K33 Says There’s No Evidence Its Cryptography Has Been Broken
